review.limitations: Not a complete book review. Later determinant/eigenvalue arguments and exercise solutions were not reviewed. The author site may offer newer builds; locators refer to the inspected fourth-edition reading copy.

sections.title: What this book provides
sections.text: A first linear-algebra text that develops proof alongside computation. The selected route explains what vectors and linear maps preserve before introducing matrices as coordinate descriptions.

sections.title: The main ideas
sections.text: A vector space carries addition and scalar multiplication satisfying explicit laws. A linear map preserves both. Such a map need not be invertible: projection can preserve linear structure while losing information.

sections.title: How the examples teach the distinction
sections.text: The text verifies closure for a line through the origin and checks projection directly. A nonzero constant offset gives a contrasting map that fails linearity. Definitions therefore distinguish superficially similar formulas.

sections.title: Why matrices enter
sections.text: A linear map is determined by its images on a basis. Express those images in the target basis and place their coordinate columns in a matrix; multiplication then computes image coordinates.

sections.title: Connection to symmetry
sections.text: Keep the abstract transformation separate from its matrix in a chosen basis. This prepares for group representations, where transformations must compose consistently and be invertible, not merely be arbitrary matrices.

terms.meaning: A map preserving addition and scalar multiplication.
A coordinate description relative to specified bases.
